technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE as the base framework for dependency upgrades.
Implement JavaMail properties integration for TLS support in the Mail sink using Spring's util:properties bean.
Leverage Avro's native compression configuration for hdfs-dataset sink to support codec customization.
Expose partitionResultsTimeout as a metadata attribute in the single-step partitioning strategy.
Use YAML-based configuration for deployment manifests to decouple from stream definitions.
Implement compression/decompression using standard libraries (e.g., GZIP, ZIP) for message modules.
Ensure backward compatibility for existing configurations when adding new compression options.
assumptions: All listed dependencies in U5 are compatible with Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE.
Existing test suites can be reused or extended for new features.
No major conflicts arise during dependency upgrades in U5.
The benchmark tool for U1 will use standard performance metrics (e.g., throughput, latency).
Compression/decompression logic for U7 and U8 will be implemented as modular components.
The deployment manifest YML file in U6 will follow Spring XD's existing configuration patterns.

activities.activity_description: Develop a benchmark tool to compare Sqoop and jdbchdfs batch jobs, including environment setup, code implementation, testing, and result analysis.
Modify hdfs-dataset sink to allow disabling Snappy compression and provide a configurable Avro codec option.
Integrate JavaMail properties (e.g., SSL/TLS settings) into the Mail sink configuration for secured IMAP/SMTP connections.
Expose partitionResultsTimeout as a metadata attribute for single-step partitioning jobs.
Upgrade Spring Boot to 1.2.0 RELEASE and update all associated dependencies listed in the specification.
Create a separate YML file for deployment manifest properties and integrate it with stream definitions.
Add gzip/zip compression and decompression options for messages in modules.
Implement compression options for Rabbit source and sink modules to enhance performance.
